html:
A Roman jurist born around 170 in Tyre, in Roman Syria. He wrote huge commentaries on the law in the time of the Severan emperors, and he is the single biggest source of Justinian's Digest, which takes about a third of its text from him.

The opening of the Digest defines justice in his words, as the constant will to give each person what is theirs. He also wrote that the emperor is not bound by the laws, a line later used to defend absolute rule.

Under Severus Alexander he became prefect of the Praetorian Guard and a leading adviser. He was strict with the guards, and they murdered him in the palace, in 223 or perhaps 228. In 426 a law of Valentinian III named him one of the five jurists whose views judges had to follow.
